answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that grows slowly over time, like a garden tended season after season: new agents start with tiny limits and earn larger ones only through consistent, useful work attested by independent peers. A sybil swarm can spin up thousands of fresh identities overnight, but it cannot fake a long horizon of honest history, and cheap identities pile up uselessly like sand on a dune while the established agents keep the valuable work. Costly patience beats cheap multiplicity.
